lisbon.title: An earthquake sparks Sparta’s helot revolt
lisbon.line: A quake devastated Sparta and its helot serfs seized the moment to revolt, a rising that took Sparta years to put down.

lisbon.title: A quake humbles Han Emperor Xuan
lisbon.line: After quakes hit 49 commanderies, Emperor Xuan called disasters Heaven’s warning, asked for frank criticism and wore plain dress for five days.

lisbon.title: Nichiren blames Japan’s rulers for disasters
lisbon.line: After a quake and famines, monk Nichiren blamed the disasters on Japan’s rulers backing teachings he called false, and was exiled.

cable.title: Byzantium’s fire beacons warn the capital
cable.line: Under Emperor Theophilos, nine hilltop fire beacons could flash warnings of Arab raids about 720 km to Constantinople within an hour.

cable.title: Chappe’s optical telegraph links Paris and Lille
cable.line: Claude Chappe’s 15 semaphore towers spanned 230 km from Lille to Paris and reported the recapture of Le Quesnoy within an hour.

krakatoa.title: Alaska’s Okmok volcano chills Rome and Egypt
krakatoa.line: Alaska’s Okmok made 43 and 42 BC among the coldest years in recent millennia, linked to failed harvests in Rome and Egypt.

krakatoa.title: Indonesia’s Samalas volcano erupts
krakatoa.line: Indonesia’s Samalas left twice Tambora’s sulfur in polar ice, and European chroniclers recorded a cold, rainy 1258 with failed harvests.

dreadnought.title: Chola India’s navy humbles Srivijaya
dreadnought.line: Rajendra Chola’s growing navy sacked Srivijaya’s capital and seized its king, breaking the trade monopoly of Southeast Asia’s leading sea power.

dreadnought.title: The Ottoman navy defeats Venice at Zonchio
dreadnought.line: The Ottomans’ growing fleet beat Venice, the eastern Mediterranean’s leading sea power, at Zonchio, marking their arrival as a serious naval force.

somme.title: Archimedes’ machines stall Rome at Syracuse
somme.line: Archimedes’ cranes and catapults wrecked Roman assaults on Syracuse, forcing a long stalemate and blockade until the city fell in 212 BC.

somme.title: The Mongol siege of Xiangyang
somme.line: Mongols besieged Song China’s twin river fortresses for nearly five years until Persian-designed counterweight trebuchets broke them in 1273.

somme.title: Ottoman cannon pound Constantinople’s walls
somme.line: Mehmed II’s giant cannon pounded Constantinople’s walls for 53 days while sappers and defenders fought in tunnels below, until the city fell.

crash.title: Florence’s great banks collapse
crash.line: Florence’s Bardi and Peruzzi banks, with branches across Europe, had lent fortunes to warring kings; defaults helped topple both by 1346.

crash.title: The South Sea Bubble bursts
crash.line: South Sea Company shares soared from £128 to £1,000 in 1720, then fell to £150 by September as Paris’s Mississippi bubble burst.

munich.title: Ivan III seizes a third of Lithuania
munich.line: Citing persecution of Orthodox believers, Ivan III, “sovereign of all Rus,” warred on Lithuania and took about a third of its land.

mccarthy.title: Han eunuchs ban scholar-officials for life
mccarthy.line: Han eunuchs had scholar-officials and about 200 students, accused of forming a faction to criticize the court, barred from office for life.

mccarthy.title: The Abbasid Mihna tests officials’ beliefs
mccarthy.line: Caliph al-Ma’mun made judges and scholars affirm that the Quran was created; refusers lost posts or were jailed, among them Ibn Hanbal.

mccarthy.title: Song China’s stone blacklist
mccarthy.line: Chancellor Cai Jing named 309 officials of a rival faction on a stone blacklist, copied across China, that sidelined them for years.

mccarthy.title: Spain’s Inquisition is founded
mccarthy.line: The Inquisition investigated converts suspected of secretly practicing Judaism, using anonymous denunciations, and barred the convicted and their descendants from office.

protests.title: Revolts sweep Europe’s cities, 1378–1382
protests.line: From Florence’s Ciompi to Ghent, England’s Peasants’ Revolt, Rouen and Paris, revolts against taxes and elites swept Europe in 1378–1382.
